patch.summary:
Choose Azure DevOps only if your buying job matches “Azure Repos/Boards/Pipelines — first 5 Basic users free, then $6/user/mo; Basic + Test Pla” rather than incident.io's shape. Choose incident.io only if your buying job matches “Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-ca” rather than Azure DevOps's shape. Workflow advantage: Azure DevOps leans source-control-devops; incident.io leans incident-oncall. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Azure DevOps is Azure Repos/Boards/Pipelines — first 5 Basic users free, then $6/user/mo; Basic + Test Plans $52/user/mo; Artifacts 2 GiB free.; incident.io is Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-call add-on +$10–$20/user. Does not outrank PagerDut.
- Company-size focus: Azure DevOps (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs incident.io (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Azure DevOps-leaning source-control-devops vs incident.io-leaning incident-oncall.
- Researched limits: Azure DevOps — User 6 onwards is $6/user/mo for every additional Basic seat — the free five are not a forever team cap workaround; incident.io — On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor.

Limitations — Azure DevOps: User 6 onwards is $6/user/mo for every additional Basic seat — the free five are not a forever team cap workaround; Test Plans at $52/user is a QA licence, not something to assign to every developer; incident.io: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor; Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award.

Poor-fit cases: Azure DevOps is a poor fit when that limitation bites: User 6 onwards is $6/user/mo for every additional Basic seat — the free five are not a forever team cap workaround · incident.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor · Avoid Azure DevOps if you actually need incident.io's motion (Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/u)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
